ai.title: Simplify CLI response handling and fix client race
ai.summary: Refactored `sendUserInputAndAwaitResponse` in `npm-app/src/cli.ts` to remove the `onStreamEnd` callback, checking for `<file>` tags post-stream instead. Updated `npm-app/src/client.ts` to skip assistant message creation if the last message is already from the assistant, preventing duplicate logs on cancelled streams. Fixed WebSocket unsubscription logic to use a single `unsubscribe()` call.

eli5.text: When the assistant stops a reply mid-way and then immediately sends a new one, the chat no longer keeps a duplicate copy of that last message in the log. Behind the scenes, the part of the app that watches the text stream and the part that stores what the assistant said were both rewritten to avoid that double-saving, and the cleanup of that stream was simplified to a single stop call instead of two. The fix is live today.

ai.title: Fix CLI escape to stop generating
ai.summary: Refactored `subscribeToResponse` in `npm-app/src/client.ts` to return a `stopResponse` closure and `responsePromise` instead of an `unsubscribe` wrapper and raw result promise. Updated `npm-app/src/cli.ts` to invoke this closure on Esc key press, replacing the manual `stopResponseRequested` flag and `responseBuffer` logic with a `wasStoppedByUser` state returned by the client. This ensures file generation stops cleanly and the CLI correctly suppresses post-processing when the user interrupts the stream.

eli5.text: When the assistant is mid-response and you press Esc, the CLI now cleanly stops generating and suppresses post-processing by invoking a stop closure returned from subscribeToResponse, replacing the old stopResponseRequested flag and responseBuffer logic with a wasStoppedByUser state propagated from the client, so file generation halts correctly without leftover handling. You would notice that interrupting with Esc now properly halts output and prevents the CLI from continuing to process or write changes after your interruption, whereas previously the manual buffer-based stop could leave post-processing running. ai.title: Fix search replace line ending handling
ai.summary: Added line ending normalization and restoration to `processFileBlock` in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. CRLF files are normalized to LF before diff generation, and original line endings are restored in the returned changes. Prevents search/replace failures on Windows files.

eli5.text: When the assistant updates a file on a Windows computer, it now handles files that use Windows-style line breaks correctly. Previously, search-and-replace operations could fail silently or produce wrong results on these files. The assistant now converts the file to a standard format while working on it, then restores the original Windows-style line breaks in the final result, so edits behave the same as on other operating systems.

ai.title: npm version 1.0.14
ai.summary: Incremented npm package version from 1.0.13 to 1.0.14 in `npm-app/package.json`.

eli5.text: The assistant's version number was bumped on the package registry, so anyone installing it fresh will pull the new build instead of the previous one. This is behind-the-scenes housekeeping to keep the published package up to date, and you won't notice any change in how the assistant behaves.
